notes.meaning: David is in danger, likely while King Saul is hunting him. Someone tells him to run off like a frightened bird to the hills. David answers that he has already taken shelter in the LORD, so why should he panic? The advice may have come from worried friends, or it may have been a mocking jab from his enemies.

These seem to be more words from those urging David to flee. The enemy is ready, with the bow bent and the arrow on the string. They plan to shoot from the dark, secretly, like someone lying in wait, at people who are honest and true. The danger was real and close.

The "foundations" are the things a nation stands on, like law, justice and honesty. Under Saul's bad rule these were breaking down. The advisers' point is that when everything is falling apart, a good person can do nothing, so he should just run. Faith answers that God is still there, as the next verse shows.

Here David gives his answer. Things on earth may be in chaos, but the LORD still sits on His throne in heaven and rules over all. He looks closely at every person, like someone narrowing their eyes to see clearly. He sees through people, not just what they do but what they think and plan.

God tests good people, the way gold is tested in a fire. He does this for their good, not because He has turned against them. But the person who loves violence, who loves to hurt the weak, God hates with His whole holy being. This is strong language for how deeply such evil goes against His goodness.

The picture recalls how God destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah with fire and sulfur from heaven. The "scorching wind" may be like the deadly hot desert wind. Their "portion" is like the share poured into their cup, meaning what God has set for them to receive. Judgment will come on the wicked suddenly, and they cannot escape it.

God acts this way because He Himself is righteous, meaning fully good and fair. So He loves what is right and just. The honest and upright will one day see His face. That means they will enjoy His loving presence and favor, the highest blessing a person can have.
